page: Amazon Web Services m5zn.12xlarge is a general-purpose, network and EBS-optimized server instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8252C processor with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a dedicated clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark data shows strong performance in memory bandwidth, with both large-block read and write operations placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression and Passmark memory scores also rank in the top 25%. However, CPU-bound benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU tests, fall within the middle 50% average. Notably, LLM inference text generation speeds for both small (135M) and medium (7B) models are weak, placing in the bottom 25%, indicating a tradeoff for complex generative AI tasks without GPU acceleration.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, making it highly suitable for network-intensive workloads. Given the high clock speed of 4.5 GHz combined with a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is well-suited for applications requiring high single-core performance, database operations, static web serving, and memory-bound processing. It offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that benefit from high-frequency Intel Xeon processors and high network throughput without requiring local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU resources.
